output.answer: Yes. USAA has announced and carried out multiple rounds of layoffs in 2026: it cut hundreds of jobs in late January 2026 as part of CEO Juan Andrade's cost-cutting reorganization, laid off 220 employees in April 2026, and confirmed another workforce reduction in early September 2026 — its second round that year and at least the seventh since March 2022. Employee posts on LinkedIn and layoff forums indicate further cuts continued into mid-October 2026. USAA did not disclose headcount for the most recent rounds, saying only that it 'regularly evaluate[s] our operations and adjust[s] to serve our members more efficiently,' while noting it filled more than 8,300 positions during the year and still employs roughly 37,000 people nationwide.
caveats: USAA has not disclosed the number of employees affected in the September 2026 round or which divisions were cut, so total 2026 layoff headcount is unconfirmed.

The October 2026 cuts and the reported plan of three bank rounds in 2026 (about 5% in January, 2.5% each in late summer and late October) come from anonymous layoff-forum posts and employees' personal LinkedIn posts, not from a USAA statement; they are plausible but unverified.

No 2026 WARN Act notice for USAA appears in public WARN trackers (the most recent Texas WARN notices listed are from 2023), consistent with the rounds being below WARN thresholds, so state filings cannot confirm the sizes.
The January 2026 P&C Specialist article is partially paywalled; the full headcount and department detail beyond the free preview could not be verified.

passages.quote: USAA has carried out another workforce reduction, marking the San Antonio company's second round of layoffs this year. The insurance and banking giant confirmed the job cuts Tuesday but refused to specify how many employees lost their positions or which divisions absorbed the blow.

Spokesperson Roger Wildermuth offered a measured explanation. "We regularly evaluate our operations and adjust to serve our members more efficiently," he said. Wildermuth added that USAA filled more than 8,300 positions this year and continues hiring as business needs evolve.
The latest cuts follow 220 layoffs in April and represent at least the seventh reduction since March 2022.
USAA slashed hundreds of jobs this week as the company continues to restructure and reduce costs, according to people familiar with the matter.

output.question: Has USAA announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: In late January 2026, USAA cut hundreds of jobs across departments including enterprise technology, bank operations, data management, anti-money laundering, marketing and service and distribution, as part of a reorganization and cost reduction under CEO Juan Andrade, who launched the restructuring in September 2025.
USAA laid off 220 employees in April 2026.

In early September 2026 USAA confirmed another round of job cuts — its second of 2026 and at least the seventh workforce reduction since March 2022 — without specifying how many employees or which divisions were affected; employees reported the cuts hit compliance, risk management and consumer lending at USAA Federal Savings Bank.

USAA spokesperson Roger Wildermuth said the company 'regularly evaluate[s] our operations and adjust[s] to serve our members more efficiently,' adding that USAA filled more than 8,300 positions in 2026 and continues hiring; the company employs roughly 37,000 people nationwide, about 17,000 in the San Antonio region.

Employee posts on LinkedIn (Oct 15, Oct 26 and Oct 30, 2026) and layoff forums indicate further USAA cuts continued into mid-to-late October 2026, including reductions across Technology and a reported final 'third round' of planned 2026 bank layoffs in late October; these are not confirmed by USAA statements.

missing_fields: Exact headcount of the September 2026 and October 2026 layoff rounds (USAA declined to specify; no official figure published).
